summary: GCP folder permission inheritance removed unexpectedly, blocking Dedicated-staging service accounts
description:
Issue summary:

Overnight we observed that several Dedicated-staging service accounts stopped being authorized to read artifacts from the shared-storage project and to list compute instances in the staging fleet. The common failure pattern is permission-denied errors for roles that should have been inherited via the folder-level IAM bindings applied at the team folder.

Impact:
- Affected internal CI/CD jobs and a subset of dedicated staging nodes failed health checks, causing degraded test rollouts.
- No customer-facing production impact identified so far, but this blocks our Dedicated onboarding flow for two upcoming demos.

Environment:
- Affected folder: projects/folders/teams-dedicated-staging (folder display name: "dedicated-staging-team")
- Affected projects: shared-storage-prod-staging, dedicated-staging-pool-eu, dedicated-staging-pool-us
- Time window: first errors observed 2026-03-10 02:14 UTC

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) CI job attempts to access gs://shared-storage-prod-staging/artifacts; received 403 permissionDenied on storage.objects.list.
2) Health-check script running on dedicated-staging node calls `gcloud compute instances list --project dedicated-staging-pool-us` and receives permissionDenied.
3) Policy Troubleshooter for a failing service account returns "No binding found" for role roles/storage.objectViewer even though the role is present at folder level in Audit logs prior to 02:00 UTC.

Observed behavior:
- Folder-level bindings that previously granted roles to group:sre-dedicated@redwood.ai are missing for multiple bindings (storage.viewer, compute.viewer).
- Audit logs show a IAM policy change around 2026-03-10 01:58 UTC with actor serviceAccount:org-admin-bot@redwood-internal.iam.gserviceaccount.com. The change was a removal of 3 bindings and an addition of a different set scoped to a single project.

Expected behavior:
- Folder-level IAM bindings should remain intact unless a deliberate retention or migration plan is executed. Changes to folder bindings should be approved via the org-iam-change pipeline.

Investigation performed so far:
- Pulled Cloud Audit Logs for `google.iam.admin.v1` and confirmed a single change event at 2026-03-10 01:58 UTC authored by org-admin-bot.
- Ran `gcloud resource-manager folders get-iam-policy` and confirmed the bindings are absent.
- Policy Troubleshooter confirms lack of effective permission on affected service accounts.
- Cross-checked terraform state in infra repo: no recent merges that would delete folder bindings; however a scheduled automation job `infra/auto-iam-migrator` had a dry-run earlier that morning according to CI history.
- Reached out to infra-automation oncall in #infra-automation Slack for context; thread indicates a failed migration attempt that retried with an unintended apply.

Temporary workaround applied:
- Manually re-applied the most-critical folder bindings (roles/storage.objectViewer, roles/compute.viewer for group:sre-dedicated@redwood.ai) to the folder at 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC. Verified that CI jobs recovered and health checks returned green.

Immediate risk and open questions:
- Need to verify whether any other folders/projects were affected by the same automation job.
- Confirm why the `auto-iam-migrator` retried with an apply and bypassed the usual approval gate.
- Assess whether service accounts that had ephemeral keys or binding-specific grants lost access permanently or if this was limited to inherited bindings only.

Proposed next steps:
1) Run a wide scan across org folders comparing current folder-level bindings to the snapshot from 2026-03-09 23:59 UTC (we have a policy-snapshot in gs://infra-iam-snapshots).
2) Rollback automation: revert last apply from `infra/auto-iam-migrator` or pause the automation until root cause is confirmed. 
3) Add an emergency guard in the automator to require manual approval when a change affects more than N folders (N=1).
4) Coordinate with Security to determine if this event requires an internal postmortem.

Resolution notes (work in progress):
- Critical bindings re-applied, services recovered. Further remediation pending org-wide scan and automator rollback.

follow_up_actions: Pause infra/auto-iam-migrator until code change merges and approval gate added
Create automated snapshot diff alert that mails #security and #infra when folder-level binding count changes > 2
Run verification job to compare gs://infra-iam-snapshots/2026-03-09-2359 against current state and produce a CSV of mismatches
Document and enforce a two-person approval for any automations that modify folder-level IAM bindings
